documents.name: Why MCP is Awesome
documents.path: WWW / Blog / Why MCP is Awesome

values.value: The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets AI assistants reach into the tools you already use — cleanly, consistently, and without a bespoke integration per app.

value.markup:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI applications talk to the tools and data sources a developer already uses. Instead of N bespoke integrations for N apps, there is one protocol and one conversation.

This matters because the real bottleneck in using AI is context: getting your models the right data at the right time. MCP standardises that hop, so a single client can reach documents, databases, design systems and content management systems alike.

values.value: A busy desk — like a busy integration surface. Every wire is a point of friction MCP removes. Photo by Christopher Gower on Unsplash.
The most powerful pattern is the one you don't have to reinvent.

value.markup:
MCP is open and community-driven. Any client can implement it, any tool can expose it, and nobody is locked in. That is what makes it stick: the protocol is the point, the vendors come and go.

If you haven't tried it yet, spin up a local MCP server for something you use every day. The first conversation is usually the best one.

values.value: MCP and Umbraco: A Match Made in the Block Grid
The Umbraco MCP server turns the management API into a conversational workspace — and this very site is the proof, blocks and all.

value.markup:
An MCP server for Umbraco wraps the management API in tools an agent can call: inspect and edit document types, create and publish content, manage media and templates. The tools are the same ones the backoffice uses — no bolts added, none removed.

That matters for a CMS because so much of the daily work is structural: a content type, a data type, a block. Doing it by hand is click-by-click. With MCP, the same work becomes a conversation.

values.value: Connected nodes, like blocks talking to blocks — and MCP talking to Umbraco. Photo by Alina Grubnyak on Unsplash.
Blocks are how content gets structure — and MCP is how structure gets made.

value.markup:
Every document type, data type, block, media item and page on this site was created through the Umbraco MCP server. No backoffice clicks, no hand-written migrations — just a conversation with the management API.

That is the demo. The block grid you are reading right now was assembled block by block, one MCP tool call at a time.
